analysis.title: "Sell The News" Or $120: Goldman Traders Lay Out The Two Ways The Oil War Premium Ends
key_insights: Goldman's oil trader says the market already prices more than $20/bbl of risk premium in Brent, while a return to all-out war would probably take Brent above $120/bbl again.
Brent traded above $112 on Thursday and hit $117/b on Friday on Houthi attacks threatening Saudi energy infrastructure, putting crude on track for a gain of about $7/bbl on the week.

Zero Hedge's own napkin math (not Goldman's) puts fundamentals-only Brent near $94 (about $114 minus $20 of premium). That implies about $20+ downside if the fear premium evaporates versus about $6+ upside to $120 in an all-out war.
Physical Middle East oil prices are falling as Hormuz flows hold up (Bloomberg). Kpler puts crude and condensate flows out of the Gulf at 24.6 million b/d, a high for the conflict.

The futures curve prices the war at full volume. Brent Dec-Jan spread hit a $4.51 backwardation, the M1-M12 spread rose $4.53 to $25.62, and the Dec-Dec spread reached $26.59, the strongest on a rolling basis on record.

Second-month Brent implied vol rose to 54.9%, the highest since mid-September, with the most bullish call skew in a month. Citi's Francesco Martoccia attributes this to demand for 'digital' options on binary geopolitical outcomes embedding event premia in nearby maturities.

Goldman's Rich Privorotsky says outcomes are highly binary. A rapid, targeted engagement with no secondary infrastructure damage could trigger an immediate 'sell the news' unwind of the risk premium. Any retaliatory disruption across key energy chokepoints would leave global balances severely constrained.

Timing: the IDF Chief of Staff reportedly sees no operational need to strike Iran before next week's Knesset election. The NYT reports the US and Israel have mapped fresh strikes after next month's US midterms. The premium therefore carries a cost every day nothing happens.

Saudi credit is under pressure. KSA was the most active CDS name with HF and real-money sellers of protection, single-name CDS across CEEMEA closed +5/+15bps wider, and Saudi bonds closed optically +10bps wider with bonds harder to source in the belly.
ENI announced a EUR1.3B extraordinary dividend and raised its buyback to EUR3.8B, triggered by refining margins well above budget (Goldman's Della Vigna: SERM revised to $18/bbl vs $6/bbl budgeted).

Goldman commodity strategists (Dart, Cyr) say Hormuz LNG disruption affects up to 300 mcm/d (19% of 2025 global LNG supply), comparable to the 330 mcm/d Russian curtailment in 2022. NW Europe starts winter with the lowest gas inventories in 14 years.

Goldman's base case for European gas is calm. Global LNG supply is still up 6% from 2022 despite a 51 mtpa drop from Qatar, thanks to an extra 55 mtpa from the US. Year-end TTF forecast is 70 EUR/MWh vs 87 now, with upside risks hedged via TTF 1Q27 call spreads.
Goldman's tight-supply/cold-winter scenario sees TTF at 150 EUR/MWh, well below the 2022 highs above 300 EUR/MWh.

The FT, relayed in Goldman's Top Stories, reports UN Ambassador Waltz acknowledged the US could still be in a stalemate with Iran a year from now. The article flags this no-war, no-peace outcome as the one nobody is pricing.
Per Privorotsky, rates have 'finally diverged from oil' this week because of the AI selloff. The article warns that if AI stabilizes while oil keeps rising, that relief disappears.

KSA CDS was the most active name, with flow skewed to hedge fund and real-money sellers.
geopolitical: Iran claimed seven tankers struck in Hormuz overnight, the largest single-day count since the war began. Goldman's EM credit desk notes the IRGC keeps making claims of tankers hitting naval mines, and the count is Iran's own.
A Houthi drone hit Shaybah. Houthis say they targeted the Saudi Defence Ministry, Aramco facilities and King Fahd airport.
The US started evacuating diplomats from Saudi Arabia.
Netanyahu flew dry-run attack formations near the Iranian border.

Iran warned that a renewed US-Israeli air campaign would bring strikes on American bases and warships and on airports, pipelines and other civilian targets across Persian Gulf neighbours (also reported by the WSJ).
The IDF Chief of Staff reportedly does not see an operational need to strike Iran before next week's Knesset election.
The NYT reports the US and Israel have mapped plans for fresh strikes on Iran after next month's US midterm elections.
The FT reports UN Ambassador Mike Waltz acknowledged the US could be in a stalemate with Iran a year from now, with no nuclear deal and no return to prewar shipping through Hormuz.
Italy approved emergency aid for truckers and farmers after diesel-price protests disrupted food deliveries, and Washington is releasing the Northeast heating oil reserve.

tension_points.bull_case: The IRGC tanker claims are even half right, the Houthis keep hitting Saudi infrastructure, and any strike touches a chokepoint. Brent above $120 becomes the starting point, and the curve and call skew already reflect this.
tension_points.bear_case: A short, surgical exchange with no secondary damage triggers a sell-the-news unwind of the more than $20/bbl premium. Physical Middle East prices are softening, Hormuz flows are at a conflict high, and the IDF and US planners reportedly are not in a hurry.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A strike that reaches pipelines, terminals or a chokepoint would invalidate the sell-the-news case. A clean, surgical strike with no secondary infrastructure damage would invalidate the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: The Hormuz LNG disruption of up to 300 mcm/d is comparable to the 2022 Russian shock, and NW Europe starts winter with the lowest inventories in 14 years.
tension_points.bear_case: Global LNG supply is up 6% from 2022 thanks to an extra 55 mtpa from the US, so Goldman forecasts TTF falling to 70 EUR/MWh by year-end.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A cold winter combined with tight supply would take TTF to 150 EUR/MWh in Goldman's scenario.
